summary: No reachable path lets candidate code read, replace, predict or influence the sealed expected reports or the reward channel: goldens live only in the verifier image under root-only /tests (0700), candidate code runs only as uid 65534 with no_new_privs, a scrubbed environment, neutral paths and an isolated interpreter via a root-owned driver copy, and reward.txt is written by root from pytest's exit status.

unread_or_truncated_ranges: tests/expected/generated.jsonl.gz and tests/expected/capacity.jsonl.gz are gzip binaries (unsupported format for the read tool); their contents were not inspected. This does not affect this axis: both are loaded by the same root-only load() path (tests/test_outputs.py:50-59) from the same 0700 /tests tree, and only their batch halves are handed to candidate code (tests/test_outputs.py:129-131), so their access boundary is fully determined by files that were read.

checks_performed: Traced agent-phase visibility: environment/Dockerfile:5-6 copies only app/ into /app and environment/.dockerignore:11-12 excludes solution/ and tests/, so no golden, sealer or verifier file exists in the candidate's working container.

Traced verifier image layout: tests/Dockerfile:5-12 copies tests into /tests, chmod 700 /tests, installs a root-owned copy of the driver at /opt/driver/tools (0644 file, 0755 dirs) and links /opt/driver/src -> /app/src; test.sh:15 re-applies chmod 700 to /tests and /logs/verifier before any candidate code runs.

Traced every candidate-code execution: reduce() (tests/test_outputs.py:86-100) and the probes (tests/test_outputs.py:209-212) all go through run_unprivileged (tests/test_outputs.py:62-83): setpriv uid/gid 65534, --clear-groups, --no-new-privs, env -i with fixed PATH/HOME/LANG, python3 -I -S, new session killed afterwards. uid 65534 cannot traverse /tests (0700 root) or /logs/verifier (0700 root).

Checked what is handed to candidate code: only row['batch'] is serialized to <mkdtemp>/batch.json (tests/test_outputs.py:92-95,131); row['report'] never leaves the root pytest process. The filename, argv, cwd (fresh mkdtemp) and environment carry no family name, test name or expected outcome.

Checked the reward channel: test.sh:4-5,20-26 writes /logs/verifier/reward.txt as root solely from pytest's exit code; candidate stdout is only parsed by json.loads and compared (tests/test_outputs.py:100,109-126), so it cannot impersonate a pass; a nonzero driver exit or timeout fails the test.

Checked root-side reads of candidate-controlled paths: test_driver_is_unchanged (tests/test_outputs.py:205-206) reads /app/tools/metalquant_run.py as root and follows symlinks, but it only yields an equality boolean inside pytest; a symlink to /tests/shipped/... could at most make that one check pass, which the candidate can achieve anyway by leaving the file unchanged, and the driver actually executed is the verifier-owned /opt/driver copy (tests/test_outputs.py:25,98). No golden bytes flow back to candidate code.

Checked test.sh:16 chmod -R a+rX /app as root: it runs after /tests is sealed; GNU chmod does not follow symlinks encountered during recursive traversal, and hard links cannot cross from the agent container into the verifier image's /tests, so a planted link cannot make goldens world-readable.

Checked pytest import/config surfaces: python3 -I -m pytest from a root-owned mktemp dir (test.sh:18-20) with cacheprovider disabled; rootdir/conftest discovery is /tests and /, neither writable by uid 65534, and /app is not on the verifier's sys.path.

Checked cross-invocation state: candidate processes can leave files in world-writable /tmp or escape killpg by re-sessioning, but still as uid 65534 without privileges; they can at most count invocations (identify batch index), which does not reveal any expected report because goldens were never candidate-visible. Stage dirs/batch files are root-owned 0755/0644 so later inputs cannot be replaced; later reduce() calls use fresh mkdtemp paths.
Checked privilege regain: --no-new-privs blocks setuid escalation from anything under /app, and no verifier step installs a candidate file as setuid.

Checked expected-value independence: goldens are precomputed and pinned by ROSTER digests (tests/test_outputs.py:39-59, tests/expected/ROSTER:1-17); nothing is derived from the submitted artifact or a candidate-provided checksum.

coverage_sweep.category: Keep expected answers and live reference implementations inaccessible to candidate code, including code the verifier executes
coverage_sweep.reason: Goldens exist only in the verifier image under /tests (0700 root); candidate code in the verifier runs as uid 65534; no reference implementation is present in either image (sealer referenced only in a docstring, not shipped); agent container excludes tests/.

coverage_sweep.category: Privileged reads of candidate-influenced paths: symlink and path-traversal escapes
coverage_sweep.reason: Only root read of a candidate path is DELIVERED_DRIVER.read_bytes() compared for equality; following a symlink yields no disclosure and no reward gain. chmod -R a+rX /app does not follow traversal symlinks and runs after sealing /tests. The executed driver is root-owned; its src symlink resolves into candidate code executed unprivileged.

coverage_sweep.category: Compute expected values independently of the submitted artifact
coverage_sweep.reason: Expected reports are sealed jsonl/gz files pinned by SHA-256 in ROSTER; comparisons use row['report'] only, never candidate output or checksums.

coverage_sweep.category: Avoid exposing hidden outcomes through filenames, arguments, working directories, or environment variables
coverage_sweep.reason: Every batch is written as batch.json in a fresh mkdtemp stage dir; cwd is another fresh mkdtemp; argv is the fixed driver path plus that file; environment is env -i with constant values. No family/test name reaches candidate code.

coverage_sweep.category: Keep grading results in a trusted channel
coverage_sweep.reason: reward.txt written by root test.sh from pytest rc into /logs/verifier (0700 root); candidate stdout is parsed and compared field by field; candidate cannot signal or ptrace root pytest.

coverage_sweep.category: Test the access boundary from the same execution context as the candidate program
coverage_sweep.reason: test_candidate_cannot_read_expected_reports and test_candidate_cannot_read_verifier_logs probe /tests/expected/ROSTER and /logs/verifier through the identical run_unprivileged wrapper used for the driver; the directory-level 0700 on /tests covers the other expected files as well.

coverage_sweep.category: Persisted / carried-over state (cache_carryover) and setuid privilege regain
coverage_sweep.reason: No phase output is trusted as a later baseline; stage files are root-owned; --no-new-privs blocks setuid regain; persisted /tmp state from uid 65534 cannot reach any answer-bearing file.

coverage_sweep.category: Colocation of oracle/reference in candidate-reachable execution path
coverage_sweep.reason: No reference solution, sealer or golden generator is present in the agent image or the verifier image's candidate-readable paths; only data goldens under 0700 /tests.

rules: Root read of delivered driver follows symlinks (tests/test_outputs.py:205-206)
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: Candidate replaces /app/tools/metalquant_run.py with a symlink to /tests/shipped/tools/metalquant_run.py; root read passes equality, but the executed driver is still /opt/driver's root-owned copy, so no answer or reward gain beyond what leaving the file unchanged gives.

rules: Package is delivered as /app/src and executed via /opt/driver/src symlink
Goldens sealed under /tests before candidate code runs
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: Candidate module in /app/src tries to open /tests/expected/*.jsonl or ROSTER during reduce(); runs as uid 65534 after test.sh:15 chmod 700 /tests, so open fails; setuid regain blocked by --no-new-privs.
Delivered /app contains a symlink pointing into /tests; recursive chmod does not dereference traversal symlinks, and it runs after the seal, so /tests stays 0700.

rules: Fixed family order of reduce() calls
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: Candidate persists an invocation counter in /tmp to learn the batch index; without golden access it cannot map index to expected report, so no hard-coded pass is possible.
